forms: name the place of a digit
which digit is in a named place
how many places a number has
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PLACE_VALUE.mastery: Given a whole number up to 999,999,999 the child names the place of any digit (ones to hundred millions), including digits beside zeros, and says which digit sits in a named place. Numbers come from real settings such as a county budget or the number of phone lines.

forms: total value of an underlined digit
total values of two digits added
difference between two digits of the same value
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.TOTAL_VALUE.mastery: Given a whole number up to 999,999,999 the child gives the total value of a chosen digit (digit times its place), adds the total values of two digits, and writes the number in expanded form. The child does not mistake a digit for its total value.

forms: read a number aloud in groups
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SYMBOLS_HM.mastery: Given a number said or written in parts (for example 45 million, 12 thousand and 7) the child writes it in figures with every place filled and zero as a place holder, and reads a figure aloud in groups of three. Numbers up to 999,999,999.

forms: choose the words for a figure
write a cheque amount in words
spot the mistake in the words
say the same number two ways
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.WORDS_FROM_.mastery: The child writes a number up to 9,999,999 in words with British spelling, a hyphen in twenty-one to ninety-nine, and each group (millions, thousands, hundreds) in order. Zeros in a group are not spoken. The design limit for words is millions.

forms: order two numbers given in words
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.FIGURES_FRO.mastery: Given a number in words up to millions, such as "two million and forty-five thousand and seven", the child writes it in figures with zero place holders in every empty place.

forms: round the same number two ways
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ROUND_TO_PL.mastery: The child rounds a number up to 999,999,999 to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, hundred thousand, million, ten million or hundred million: looks at the digit just to the right, rounds up on 5 or more, and writes zeros in all places after the one rounded.

forms: round the number in a report
why a rounded number is not exact
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ROUND_IN_CO.mastery: Given a real setting (a population, a county budget, a news report) the child chooses the sensible place to round to, rounds the number, and says why the rounded number is only an estimate. Rounding a carried digit (such as 999,500 to the nearest thousand) is included.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.EVEN_ODD.mastery: The child classifies any whole number up to millions as even or odd by its last digit, and knows that sums and products of even and odd numbers follow a pattern (even + even is even, odd + odd is even, even x anything is even).

forms: pick the primes from a table
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PRIME_NUMBE.mastery: The child tells prime from composite numbers up to 100 by testing small divisors, knows that 1 is neither, that 2 is the only even prime, and that an odd number is not always prime. The child lists the primes up to 50.

forms: sum or difference in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ADD_SUB_LAR.mastery: The child adds and subtracts whole numbers of up to nine digits in a column, regrouping across zeros, and decides whether to add or subtract in a story about money, population or distance. Answers are checked by estimating.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.MULT_LARGE.mastery: The child multiplies a number of up to 4 digits by a number of up to 3 digits using long multiplication, with the zero place holder in the second and third rows, and by 10, 100 and 1,000 by shifting the digits. The product is checked by estimating.

forms: what the remainder means in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.DIV_LARGE.mastery: The child divides a number of up to 6 digits by a number of up to 3 digits by long division, with zeros in the quotient where a digit does not fit, writes the remainder as a whole number, and checks by multiplying back.

forms: put in brackets to make a value
find the mistake in the order
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ORDER_OF_OP.mastery: The child works out expressions of up to three operations with brackets, working brackets first, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. Numbers up to 3 digits.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.OPERATIONS_.mastery: The child reads a story with two or three steps (fares, fuel, rent, bags and rows), chooses the operations, works them in order and writes the answer with its unit. Money left, total takings and equal sharing are included.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_EXTEND_.mastery: Given the first four to six terms of a sequence with a constant difference or a constant multiplier, the child finds the rule, continues the sequence, and spots a term that does not fit.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_NTH_TER.mastery: For a sequence that goes up or down by the same amount, the child finds a distant term (for example the 12th) by first term plus the number of steps times the difference, and does not count the first term as a step.

forms: write the terms from a rule
MATH.G7.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SEQ_CREATE_.mastery: Given a rule such as "start at 5, add 4" or "multiply by 3 then add 3", the child writes the first terms, and makes a sequence of their own for a number game, checking that the terms follow the rule every time.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.DIV_BY_2_4_8_5_10.mastery: The child tests a number up to 6 digits for divisibility by 2, 5 and 10 from the last digit, by 4 from the last two digits and by 8 from the last three digits, and explains the test.

forms: divisible by 6: count from a table
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.DIV_BY_3_6_9.mastery: The child adds the digits of a number up to 6 digits and tests the sum for 3 and 9, and knows a number is divisible by 6 only when it is even and divisible by 3.

forms: spot the slip in the working
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.DIV_BY_11.mastery: The child adds the digits in the odd places and in the even places, subtracts the two sums, and says the number is divisible by 11 when the difference is 0 or a multiple of 11.

forms: find the mistake in the working
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.PRIME_FACTORISE.mastery: The child splits a number up to 500 with a factor tree or repeated division by 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 until every factor is prime, writes repeated factors in full or with a power, and explains why a number with no small factors may still be composite.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.GCD_BY_FACTORS.mastery: The child writes each of two or three numbers (up to 200) as a product of primes, multiplies the primes common to all of them, taking each as many times as it is in every number, and gets the GCD.

forms: why the product is not the least
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.LCM_BY_FACTORS.mastery: The child writes each of two or three numbers (up to 60) as a product of primes and multiplies each prime the greatest number of times it appears in any one number, and gets the LCM.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.GCD_IN_CONTEXT.mastery: The child decides from a story that the greatest equal size or number of equal groups is the GCD (cutting ropes, packing boxes, tiling) and works it out for two or three quantities, answering the size or the number asked.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FACTORS.LCM_IN_CONTEXT.mastery: The child decides from a story that the first time two or three repeating events coincide is the LCM (matatus leaving, bells ringing) and works it out in minutes or days, answering the time asked.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.COMPARE_FRACTIO.mastery: The child compares two or three fractions with denominators up to 12 by renaming them with a common denominator, decides which is greater, orders them, and can explain why a bigger denominator does not mean a bigger fraction.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.ADD_UNLIKE_FRAC.mastery: The child adds two fractions or mixed numbers with unlike denominators (up to 12) by renaming with the LCM, adds numerators, carries any whole from the fraction part, and writes the sum in simplest form.

forms: what is left in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.SUBTRACT_UNLIKE.mastery: The child subtracts fractions or mixed numbers with unlike denominators (up to 12) by renaming with the LCM, regroups a whole into the fraction part when needed, reduces the whole by one, and simplifies.

forms: multiply a fraction by a whole number
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.MULT_FRACTION_B.mastery: The child multiplies a fraction by a whole number (and finds a fraction of a quantity), multiplying the numerator and keeping the denominator, simplifies, and writes an improper result as a mixed number.

The child multiplies a fraction by a fraction or a mixed number by writing mixed numbers as improper fractions, multiplying numerators and denominators, simplifying (also across before multiplying), and finds a fraction of a fraction of an amount in a story.

forms: use a reciprocal in a story
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.RECIPROCAL.mastery: The child writes the reciprocal by turning a fraction upside down, writes a whole number as a fraction over 1 first, writes a mixed number as an improper fraction first, and checks that the number times its reciprocal is 1.

forms: divide a fraction by a whole number
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.DIVIDE_FRACTION.mastery: The child divides a fraction or a mixed number by a whole number by multiplying the denominator (or by the reciprocal), simplifies, and knows the result is smaller than the fraction.

forms: divide a fraction by a fraction
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.DIVIDE_BY_FRACT.mastery: The child divides a whole number, fraction or mixed number by a fraction or a mixed number by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor (the second number only), writing mixed numbers as improper fractions first.

forms: divide a whole number by a fraction
will the answer be larger or smaller
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.DIVIDE_WHOLE_BY.mastery: The child divides a whole number by a fraction, chooses division when the story asks how many small amounts fit into a large one (cups from a jug, bags from a sack), and knows the answer is larger than the whole number.

forms: a whole number as a term
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_SEQ_AD.mastery: The child finds the constant gap between terms of a sequence of fractions with a common denominator, keeps the denominator, and writes the next terms and a term that is a whole number as a fraction.

forms: spot the term that does not fit
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_SEQ_MU.mastery: The child finds that terms such as 1, 1/3, 1/9 follow a constant ratio, states the rule (divide by 3, or multiply by 1/3), and continues the sequence.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_SEQ_IN.mastery: Given a table of the part of a task done after equal times (2, 4, 6 hours), the child finds the part done per step, and answers when the task is complete or how much is done at a later time, counting hours and not steps.

forms: write the first terms from a rule
MATH.G7.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_SEQ_CR.mastery: The child writes a sequence of fractions from a rule (add 1/4, or multiply by 1/2), keeps every term in line with the rule, and writes a rule for a puzzle sequence of their own that a partner can solve.

forms: write the number from a chart
which digit is in the place
MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DEC_PLACE_AND_TO.mastery: The child names the place of a digit after the point (tenths, hundredths, thousandths), gives its total value (the 7 in 4.073 is worth 0.07), and writes a decimal from a place value chart whose rows are not in order.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DEC_COUNT_TENTHS.mastery: The child says how many tenths (or hundredths) make a decimal such as 7.7 (77 tenths) by counting the whole ones as ten tenths each.

forms: find the mistake with the point
MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.MULT_DEC_BY_WHOL.mastery: The child multiplies a decimal with up to three places by a whole number up to 100 by multiplying without the point and putting the point back with the same number of places, and decides if the answer is sensible.

forms: is the product bigger or smaller
MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.MULT_DEC_BY_DEC.mastery: The child multiplies two decimals by multiplying without points and giving the product as many decimal places as both factors together, uses it for the area of a rectangle with decimal sides, and says when the product is smaller than a factor.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DIV_DEC_BY_WHOLE.mastery: The child divides a decimal by a whole number, and a whole number by a whole number with a decimal quotient (12 / 8 = 1.5), by long division with the point in the quotient directly above the point in the dividend.

MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DIV_BY_DECIMAL.mastery: The child divides by a decimal by moving the point in both numbers the same number of places until the divisor is whole, uses it to count how many small amounts fit into a large one, and finds a price per kilogram.

forms: why is the answer bigger than 6
MATH.G7.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DEC_DIVISION_SIZ.mastery: The child says that dividing by a number less than 1 makes the answer larger and dividing by a number greater than 1 makes it smaller, using how many lots fit, and does not move the point without a reason.

forms: square of a multiple of ten
MATH.G7.NUMBER.SQUARES_AND_SQUARE_ROOTS..mastery: The child finds the square of a whole number up to 50, and of multiples of 10 (30 squared is 900), by multiplying the number by itself, and knows that squaring is not doubling.
The child squares a fraction by multiplying the numerator by itself and the denominator by itself, simplifies, and says why the answer is smaller than the fraction.

The child squares a decimal such as 0.03 or 1.5 by multiplying without the point and giving the square twice as many decimal places, and uses it for the area of a square plot and for the area when the side is doubled.
The child finds the square root of a perfect square up to 2,500 by finding the number that multiplied by itself gives it, checks by squaring, and knows the root of a sum is not the sum of the roots.

The child finds the root of a fraction by taking the root of the numerator and of the denominator (9/16 gives 3/4), and of a decimal that is a perfect square (0.09 gives 0.3 and 1.44 gives 1.2) by halving the decimal places.
The child takes the square root of the area of a square plot to find a side, then uses the side (for the distance round, or to compare plots), reading the question to know which is needed.

forms: which perfect squares are either side
MATH.G7.NUMBER.SQUARES_AND_SQUARE_ROOTS..mastery: The child finds the two perfect squares either side of a number (98 lies between 81 and 100) and so places its root between two whole numbers (between 9 and 10). The number is not itself a perfect square: this skill supports checking roots.
